description: SIFTEC compat suite, offered only when SIFTEC is loaded. Uses SIFTEC's own test commands (op needed).

scenes.title: SIFTEC factory: the buildings_a row of work-package-5 buildings (built once, marked by bedrock at 1190 160 970)
setup: execute in minecraft:overworld run forceload add 1180 960 1290 1040
execute in minecraft:overworld unless block 1190 160 970 minecraft:bedrock run siftec worldtest buildings_a view 0
execute in minecraft:overworld run setblock 1190 160 970 minecraft:bedrock
scenes.requiresNote: Builds SIFTEC's buildings_a row with SIFTEC's test command (siftec worldtest), which lives in SIFTEC's CI-only selftest mod, not in its release.

scenes.title: The Sift (Mielon's The Sift dimension; its own clock and weather pinned too)
setup: execute in the_sift:the_sift run time set 6000
execute in the_sift:the_sift run weather clear
execute in the_sift:the_sift positioned 0.5 0 0.5 positioned over motion_blocking run tp @a ~ ~4 ~ 45 20
scenes.ciVanillaDrawGateReason: Its average follows the runner's frame rate: below 20 fps every frame lines up with a game tick and draws the tick's extra draws, above it some don't. Run 40180107484, full: Brimstone 154.0 average / 154 median at 15.1 fps, vanilla's measure run 135.58 / 154 at 22.64 fps (Vulkan: 153.97 / 154 at 15.8 fps against 153.94 / 154 at 12.37 fps). Gated against vanilla on the median (Andre's rule, 2026-10-25).
scenes.ciNote: Mob spawning is off for this scene and the mobs already there are sent away before it settles, in vanilla's runs and Brimstone's alike: Andre's decision (package 3, 2026-10-25), as the sprites over the canyon were somewhere else in every run; they turned out to be the Sift's note particles, which CI's pin mod holds off (SiftParticlesMixin). The next scene turns spawning back on.

screen.prompt: Right-click the HUB in front of you

scenes.ciVanillaDrawGateReason: Its average follows the runner's frame rate (the GUI screen draws more per frame when frames line up with game ticks). run 40238316211, Vulkan: Brimstone 132.6 average / 162 median at 25.17 fps, vanilla's measure run 117.94 / 162 at 29.31 fps (limit x 1.10 + 2: 131.73); full on the same run: 116.03 / 162 against 116.48 / 162 at 29.83 fps both. Gated against vanilla on the median (Andre's rule, 2026-10-26).

scenes.title: SIFTEC fullscreen map, centred on a pinned player
scenes.ciNoStrict: SIFTEC's map shows whichever tiles it has scanned when it opens, so vanilla runs differ from each other by up to 22,532 strict pixels there (35-58k pixels in all after two attempts to wait for a steady map); package 7 (GUI) must give it real strict coverage
scenes.requiresNote: SIFTEC's map unlocks through progression; its test command (siftec worldtest map) opens it, and that lives in SIFTEC's CI-only selftest mod, not in its release.

scenes.title: SIFTEC Build Gun hologram (green where the building fits) in front of a water pool, high above the terrain (package 3)
setup: item replace entity @a weapon.mainhand with minecraft:air
item replace entity @a weapon.mainhand with siftec:build_gun
scenes.ciNote: The Build Gun hologram is drawn by Create's outliner (SIFTEC's BuildGunClient), not as terrain, so it stays on its own path; the gates check that it still looks exactly as with vanilla in front of Brimstone's translucent water. CI presses Tab once after the setup (the Build Gun's next-tab key: picks the first Power building, the Power Pole Mk.1; the selection stays for the bench). On a laptop, press Tab once with the Build Gun in hand before the bench starts measuring. The pool's floor is sea lanterns: up there water freezes over at random where block light is low (ice in vanilla's own runs, run 40121527770), and light 14 at the surface stops it. The last setup step moves the camera three blocks, so vanilla sorts the water again from where the picture is taken. Not run on Vulkan: lavapipe segfaults (libvulkan_lvp.so) as soon as the outliner draws, in vanilla's run too (runs 40115084815 and 40119107821).
scenes.ciSkipReason: Mesa's lavapipe Vulkan driver segfaults drawing Create's outliner (the hologram), in vanilla's run too

scenes.title: Create connected textures: walls of andesite casing (with a corner), brass casing, copper casing with a stone block set in it, and framed glass, each beside a non-connecting block (stone, glass) (package 4)
scenes.requiresNote: Create's casings and framed glass: without Create the scene would show only stone, so it is skipped.
scenes.ciNote: The design doc's done-when names Create's connected textures: Create draws them through the Fabric Renderer API, so these blocks are tessellated by Brimstone's renderer in Brimstone's runs and by Indigo in the vanilla runs. CT blocks in view: create:andesite_casing (a 5x4 wall plus a 3-block return at its west end), create:brass_casing (a 5x4 wall and a 3x3 floor patch in front), create:copper_casing (a 5x4 wall with minecraft:stone set in at its centre left), create:framed_glass (a 5x4 wall); each wall ends against minecraft:stone or minecraft:glass, which do not connect. CI presses F1 after the setup (vanilla's hide-GUI key): SIFTEC's minimap shows whichever tiles it has scanned, which differs from run to run (vanilla against vanilla up to 167 strict pixels in run 40274749083), and a single wrong connected-texture border is smaller than that. It is the suite's last scene, so the hidden GUI reaches only its own bench.
